correctness.rationale: For all m>=2, rank m+1 is immediate from columns (1,a) over all a. A width-two syndrome is exactly zero, any odd (1,a), or an even adjacent XOR. In both window models the XOR of all nonzero field elements vanishes, whereas full adjacent-XOR coverage would contradict telescoping (one duplicated label in the cyclic case). The explicit primitive-power order supplies q-2 distinct differences, misses Delta=(1+alpha)alpha^(q-2), and has adjacent end edges already in the list; alpha^j+alpha^(j+2)=Delta with j=q-2-t closes the gap in a three-window, including m=2. Actual packaged verifier checks degrees 2..8 and 6+5040 small normalized orderings. Finite checks support but cannot replace all-rank algebraic proof.

value.rationale: A motivated exact structural invariant for a recently defined burst-covering setting: localized parity-check access depends on coordinate order unlike Hamming covering radius. The theorem settles optimal width uniformly for the entire extended Hamming family, sharpens this by one-syndrome exact two-window deficiency for every ordering, and gives a single explicit all-size sequence and boundary-robust proof. It is neither a table lookup nor a new notation for a one-off computation; the original article only gives m=3 and asks for additional code families.
